knowledge_statements.statement_title: MPEC-ACQ and MPEC-GCQ
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines MPEC versions of the Abadie and Guignard constraint qualifications using tangent and linearized tangent cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let z be feasible for the MPEC. The MPEC is said to satisfy MPEC-ACQ at z if \mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}(z)=\mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(z). It is said to satisfy MPEC-GCQ at z if \mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}(z)^\circ=\bigl(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(z)\bigr)^\circ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible MPEC point, MPEC-ACQ holds when the MPEC tangent cone equals its linearized tangent cone. MPEC-GCQ holds when the polar cones of those two cones are equal.
assumptions_latex: z\text{ is feasible for the MPEC}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{MPEC\text{-}ACQ}:\ \mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}(z)=\mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(z);\qquad \mathrm{MPEC\text{-}GCQ}:\ \mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}(z)^\circ=\bigl(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{MPEC}}^{\mathrm{lin}}(z)\bigr)^\circ.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partitionwise multiplier characterization of MPEC stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient stationarity characterization under global homeomorphism of the linearized map; the multipliers may depend on the partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u^*=(x^*,y^*,w^*,z^*)\in\mathcal F\), and suppose \(LH^*\) is a global homeomorphism. Then \(u^*\) is stationary for problem (1) if and only if, for every partition \((\beta_1,\beta_2)\) of \(\beta\), there exist \(\zeta\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(\pi\in\mathbb R^{m+\ell}\) such that \[df_x^*-(DF_x)^T\pi+G^T\zeta=0,\quad df_{y_\alpha}^*-(DF_{y_\alpha})^T\pi=0,\quad df_{w_\gamma}^*-(DF_{w_\gamma})^T\pi=0,\] \[df_{y_{\beta_1}}^*-(DF_{y_{\beta_1}})^T\pi\geq0,\qquad df_{w_{\beta_2}}^*-(DF_{w_{\beta_2}})^T\pi\geq0,\] \[\zeta\geq0,\qquad \zeta^T(a-Gx^*)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point where the linearized map is a global homeomorphism, stationarity is equivalent to the existence, separately for every partition of the biactive index set, of multipliers satisfying the displayed equations, inequalities, and complementary-slackness condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u^*\text{ is stationary for (1)}\iff \forall(\beta_1,\beta_2)\text{ partitioning }\beta,\ \exists\zeta\in\mathbb R^p,\ \pi\in\mathbb R^{m+\ell}\text{ satisfying the displayed system}.

At a feasible point z-bar satisfying h(z-bar)=0, assume SBCQ, convexity of every g_i(x,·) on the stated projected domain, and the specified tangent-to-linearization inclusion for some multiplier subset M′. If, for every multiplier in M′ and every required partition of the degenerate index set, matrix (6) is nonsingular and system (7) is solvable, then the tangent and linearization cones coincide. Thus the MPEC basic constraint qualification holds with M′.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: RNLP Strong Second-Order Sufficient Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines RNLP-SSOSC using uniform positive Lagrangian curvature on the strong RNLP direction set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let z^* be strongly stationary with multipliers (\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*). RNLP-SSOSC holds if there exists \omega>0 such that d^T\nabla_{zz}^2\mathcal L(z^*,\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*)d\geq\omega for every nonzero d\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{RNLP}}^{\mathrm S}(z^*).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a strongly stationary point with fixed multipliers, RNLP-SSOSC holds when the Lagrangian Hessian quadratic form is at least a positive constant for every nonzero direction in the strong RNLP critical direction set.
assumptions_latex: z^*\text{ is strongly stationary with multipliers }(\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^T\nabla_{zz}^2\mathcal L(z^*,\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*)d\geq\omega\quad\forall d\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{RNLP}}^{\mathrm S}(z^*)\setminus\{0\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MFCQ for a parameterized lower-level inequality system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MFCQ at a feasible lower-level point, its alternative characterization, and its convex equivalence to Slater strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At $y\in C(x)$, with active set $\mathcal I(x,y)=\{i:g_i(x,y)=0\}$, MFCQ holds if there exists $v$ such that $v^T\nabla_y g_i(x,y)<0$ for every $i\in\mathcal I(x,y)$. Equivalently, $\sum_{i\in\mathcal I(x,y)}\lambda_i\nabla_y g_i(x,y)=0$ and $\lambda_i\ge0$ imply $\lambda_i=0$ for all active $i$; equivalently, the associated multiplier set $M(x,y)$ is nonempty and bounded. If every $g_i(x,\cdot)$ is convex, MFCQ is equivalent to the existence of $\bar y$ satisfying $g(x,\bar y)<0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ requires a direction that strictly decreases every active lower-level inequality. It is equivalent to exclusion of a nonzero nonnegative abnormal multiplier and to nonemptiness and boundedness of the associated multiplier set. For convex lower-level inequalities, it is equivalent to Slater strict feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the Slater equivalence, each }g_i(x,\cdot)\text{ is convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MFCQ}(x,y)\iff\left[\sum_{i\in\mathcal I(x,y)}\lambda_i\nabla_y g_i(x,y)=0,\ \lambda\ge0\Rightarrow\lambda=0\right],\quad\text{and under convexity }\operatorname{MFCQ}(x,y)\iff\exists\bar y:\ g(x,\bar y)<0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers LICQ to all branches induced by zero-multiplier active indices and derives MPEC stationarity when system (12) is solvable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose $(\bar x,\bar y,\bar\lambda)\in\mathcal F^{\mathrm{KKT}}$ and LICQ holds for $(11)$ at this triple. knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonexistence criterion ensuring metric-subregularity constraint qualification at a feasible MPEC point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be feasible for the MPEC. Assume there are no $(u,v)\ne0$, $\lambda\in\bar\Lambda(v)\cap\overline{\mathcal E}$, and $w\ne0$ satisfying simultaneously
\[
-\nabla^2_{yx}f(\bar x,\bar y)u-\nabla^2_{yy}f(\bar x,\bar y)v-\nabla^2(\lambda^Tg)(\bar y)v\in N_{\bar K_\Gamma}(v),
\]
\[
\nabla^2_{xy}f(\bar x,\bar y)w=0,
\qquad
\nabla g_i(\bar y)^Tw=0\quad(i\in\bar J^+(\lambda)),
\]
\[
w^T\bigl(\nabla^2_{yy}f(\bar x,\bar y)+\nabla^2(\lambda^Tg)(\bar y)\bigr)w\le0.
\]
Then MSCQ for the MPEC holds at $(\bar x,\bar y)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible MPEC point, MSCQ holds if no nonzero directions and admissible multiplier jointly satisfy the displayed second-order normal-cone inclusion, kernel and active-gradient orthogonality equations, and nonpositive curvature condition.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is feasible for the MPEC}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{MSCQ}\text{ holds for the MPEC at }(\bar x,\bar y).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized linear-independence qualification implies S-stationarity for an MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S-stationarity condition for the MPEC reformulation of a bilevel program with a convex lower-level problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\bar x,\bar y)\) be a local minimizer of \((\mathrm{MPEC})\) satisfying MSCQ, and define \(P(x,y):=(y,-\nabla_y f(x,y))\). If
\[
\nabla P(\bar x,\bar y)\mathbb R^{n+m}+\mathcal L\!\left(T_{\operatorname{gph}N_\Gamma}(P(\bar x,\bar y))\right)=\mathbb R^{2m},
\]
where \(\mathcal L\) denotes the generalized linearity space, then \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is S-stationary for \((\mathrm{MPEC})\): there exists \(w\) such that
\[
0=\nabla_xF(\bar x,\bar y)+\nabla_{xy}^2f(\bar x,\bar y)w,
\]
\[
0\in\nabla_yF(\bar x,\bar y)+\nabla_{yy}^2f(\bar x,\bar y)w+\widehat D N_\Gamma\!\left(\bar y,-\nabla_yf(\bar x,\bar y)\right)(w).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an MSCQ local minimizer, the stated generalized linear-independence condition for the mapping P and the tangent cone to the graph of the lower-level normal-cone mapping guarantees S-stationarity and the displayed stationarity system.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local minimizer of }(\mathrm{MPEC})
\nabla P(\bar x,\bar y)\mathbb R^{n+m}+\mathcal L\!\left(T_{\operatorname{gph}N_\Gamma}(P(\bar x,\bar y))\right)=\mathbb R^{2m}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is S-stationary for }(\mathrm{MPEC})\text{ and admits }w\text{ satisfying the displayed system.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adjoint-based necessary condition for a strongly regular generalized-equation MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary stationarity condition for a local MPEC solution whose equilibrium solution map is defined by a strongly regular generalized equation; notation is inherited from the source formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})$ be a local solution of the MPEC (7.1), with $S$ defined by the generalized equation (7.19) with $z=y$. Assume that this generalized equation is strongly regular at $(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})$ and that, for every $i\in\mathbb K(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})$, $\widehat\pi_i$ is the unique solution of
\[
\bigl(\mathcal J_yF_{L\cup(I^0\setminus M_i),\,L\cup(I^0\setminus M_i)}\bigr)^T\pi_i-\bigl(\nabla_y f(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})\bigr)_{L\cup(I^0\setminus M_i)}=0.
\]
Then
\[
0\in \nabla_x f(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})-\operatorname{conv}\left\{\bigl(\mathcal J_xF_{L\cup(I^0\setminus M_i)}(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})\bigr)^T\widehat\pi_i\mid i\in\mathbb K(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})\right\}+K_{U_{\mathrm{ad}}}(\widehat{x}).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local solution of the specified MPEC, strong regularity of the defining generalized equation and unique solvability of every indexed adjoint equation imply the stated convex-hull stationarity inclusion involving the x-gradient, adjoint Jacobian terms, and the set associated with the admissible region.
assumptions_latex: (\widehat{x},\widehat{y})\text{ is a local solution of MPEC (7.1), with }S\text{ defined by generalized equation (7.19) and }z=y.
\text{The generalized equation is strongly regular at }(\widehat{x},\widehat{y}).

\forall i\in\mathbb K(\widehat{x},\widehat{y}),\ \widehat\pi_i\text{ is the unique solution of }\bigl(\mathcal J_yF_{L\cup(I^0\setminus M_i),\,L\cup(I^0\setminus M_i)}\bigr)^T\pi_i-\bigl(\nabla_y f(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})\bigr)_{L\cup(I^0\setminus M_i)}=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic, Extreme, and Full MPEC Constraint Qualifications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions and implications for multiplier-indexed tangent-linearization constraint qualifications at an MPEC-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar z=(\bar x,\bar y)\in\mathcal F\). The basic CQ holds at \(\bar z\) if there exists a nonempty set \(M'\subseteq M(\bar z)\) such that \[\mathcal T(\bar z;\mathcal F)=\mathcal L'(\bar z;\mathcal F),\qquad \mathcal L'(\bar z;\mathcal F):=\mathcal T(\bar z;Z)\cap\bigcup_{\lambda\in M'}\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal{LS}_{(\bar z,\lambda)}).\] The extreme CQ and full CQ are obtained by requiring this equality with \(M'=M^e(\bar z)\) and \(M'=M(\bar z)\), respectively. If \(M(\bar z)\) is a singleton, the three CQs coincide. In general, \(\mathrm{extreme\ CQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{basic\ CQ}\), and, provided CRCQ holds, \(\mathrm{full\ CQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{extreme\ CQ}\). The basic CQ holds for MPAECs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible MPEC point, the basic CQ equates the feasible tangent cone with a multiplier-indexed linearization formed from some nonempty subset of multipliers. Using all extreme multipliers defines the extreme CQ, while using all multipliers defines the full CQ. The three coincide when the multiplier set is a singleton. Extreme CQ implies basic CQ, and full CQ implies extreme CQ under CRCQ. The basic CQ holds for MPAECs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{extreme\ CQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{basic\ CQ},\qquad \mathrm{CRCQ}+\mathrm{full\ CQ}\Rightarrow\mathrm{extreme\ CQ}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonqualified multiplier conditions for an abstract MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fritz John-type upper- and lower-subdifferential necessary conditions without the mixed MPEC qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution of the abstract MPEC. Assume that $X,Y$ are Asplund spaces, $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, and $\Omega$ is locally closed around $\bar x$. If either $S$ is PSNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$ or $\Omega$ is SNC at $\bar x$, then there exists $\lambda\in\{0,1\}$ such that, for every $(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)$, there exist
\[
x_1^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(\lambda y^*),\qquad x_2^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega)
\]
satisfying
\[
\lambda x^*+x_1^*+x_2^*=0,
\qquad (\lambda,x_1^*)\ne(0,0).
\]
If, in addition, $\varphi$ is locally Lipschitz around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, then there exist $\lambda\geq0$, $(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)$, $x_1^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(\lambda y^*)$, and $x_2^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega)$ satisfying the same equation and nontriviality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without the mixed qualification, a local abstract-MPEC solution still satisfies a nontrivial Fritz John-type coderivative-normal condition. One multiplier in {0,1} works for all upper regular subgradients; if the objective is locally Lipschitz, an existential limiting-subgradient version holds with a nonnegative multiplier.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local solution of the abstract MPEC}
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y)
S\text{ is PSNC at }(\bar x,\bar y)\ \lor\ \Omega\text{ is SNC at }\bar x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda\in\{0,1\}\ \forall(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\ \exists x_1^*,x_2^*:\ x_1^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(\lambda y^*),\ x_2^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega),\ \lambda x^*+x_1^*+x_2^*=0,\ (\lambda,x_1^*)\ne(0,0),\text{ together with the stated locally-Lipschitz limiting-subgradient extension}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-CQ Multiplier Characterization of MPEC Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A model-specific primal–dual stationarity characterization for the MPEC denoted (13).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^{n+m}\to\mathbb R\) and \(F:\mathbb R^{n+m}\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(Z\) be given by (3), and suppose the full CQ (2) holds for MPEC (13) at \(\bar z\in\mathcal F\). Then \(\bar z\) is stationary if and only if, for every \(\beta_1\subseteq\beta(\bar z)\), there exist \(\zeta\in\mathbb R^s\) and \(\pi\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(\nabla_x f(\bar z)+G^T\zeta-\nabla_xF(\bar z)^T\pi=0\); \(\partial_{y_i}f(\bar z)+H_i^T\zeta-\sum_{j=1}^m\pi_j\partial_{y_i}F_j(\bar z)=0\) for \(i\in\alpha(\bar z)\); the same expression is nonnegative for \(i\in\beta(\bar z)\setminus\beta_1\); \(\pi_i\ge0\) for \(i\in\beta_1\); \(\pi_i=0\) for \(i\in\gamma(\bar z)\); and \(\zeta\ge0\), \(\zeta^T(G\bar x+H\bar y+a)=0\), where \(H_i\) is the \(i\)-th column of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the full constraint qualification, a feasible point is stationary exactly when every subset of its degenerate indices admits multipliers satisfying the stated stationarity, sign, zero-pattern, and complementarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar z\text{ is stationary}\iff \forall\beta_1\subseteq\beta(\bar z),\;\exists(\zeta,\pi)\in\mathbb R^s\times\mathbb R^m\text{ satisfying system (14) and its accompanying sign, zero-pattern, and complementarity conditions}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: RNLP-SOSC and MPEC-SOSC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the RNLP and MPEC second-order sufficient conditions by the direction set on which uniform positive Lagrangian curvature is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let z^* be strongly stationary with multipliers (\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*). RNLP-SOSC holds if there exists \omega>0 such that d^T
abla_{zz}^2\mathcal L(z^*,\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*)d\geq\omega for every nonzero d\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{RNLP}}(z^*). MPEC-SOSC holds when the same inequality is required instead for every nonzero d\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MPEC}}(z^*), where \mathcal C_{\mathrm{MPEC}}(z^*):=\mathcal C_{\mathrm{RNLP}}(z^*)\cap\{d\mid \min(
abla G_j(z^*)^Td,
abla H_j(z^*)^Td)=0\  orall j\in\mathcal D(z^*)	ext{ with }\widehat v_{1j}^*=\widehat v_{2j}^*=0\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a strongly stationary point with fixed multipliers, RNLP-SOSC requires the Lagrangian Hessian quadratic form to be at least a positive constant on every nonzero RNLP critical direction. MPEC-SOSC imposes the same requirement on the specified smaller MPEC direction set.
assumptions_latex: z^*\text{ is strongly stationary with multipliers }(\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^T\nabla_{zz}^2\mathcal L(z^*,\lambda^*,\widehat v_1^*,\widehat v_2^*)d\geq\omega\quad\forall d\neq0\text{ in the applicable direction set}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Abstract MPEC conditions under a Lipschitz-like equilibrium mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper- and lower-subdifferential stationarity conditions obtained from Lipschitz-like regularity of the equilibrium mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution of the abstract MPEC in Asplund spaces $X,Y$. Suppose $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\Omega$ is locally closed around $\bar x$, and $S$ is Lipschitz-like around $(\bar x,\bar y)$. Then
\[
\forall(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\qquad -x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).
\]
If, in addition, $\varphi$ is locally Lipschitz around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, then
\[
\exists(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\qquad -x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a local abstract-MPEC solution, a Lipschitz-like equilibrium mapping gives the coderivative-normal inclusion for every upper regular subgradient. If the objective is also locally Lipschitz, the inclusion holds for some limiting subgradient.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local solution of the abstract MPEC}
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y)
S\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar y)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall(x^*,y^*)\in\widehat\partial^{+}\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\ -x^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega);\quad \varphi\text{ locally Lipschitz}\Rightarrow\exists(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\text{ satisfying the same inclusion}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent cone and stationarity under BIF
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the feasible tangent cone and first-order stationarity of an MPEC whose local equilibrium response satisfies BIF.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be convex and let $(\bar x,\bar y)\in\mathcal F$. Under BIF, $$\mathcal T((\bar x,\bar y);\mathcal F)=\{(d_x,d_y)\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)\times\mathbb R^m:d_y=y'(\bar x;d_x)\}.$$ Consequently, $(\bar x,\bar y)$ is stationary if and only if, for every $d_x\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)$, $$\nabla_x f(\bar x,\bar y)^Td_x+\nabla_y f(\bar x,\bar y)^Ty'(\bar x;d_x)\ge 0.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the upper-level set is convex and the equilibrium response satisfies BIF, each feasible tangent direction is exactly a parameter tangent direction paired with the directional derivative of the implicit response. The point is stationary if and only if the induced objective directional derivative is nonnegative for every parameter tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal T((\bar x,\bar y);\mathcal F)=\{(d_x,y'(\bar x;d_x)):d_x\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X)\},\quad (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ stationary}\iff \forall d_x\in\mathcal T(\bar x;X),\;\nabla_x f^Td_x+\nabla_y f^Ty'(\bar x;d_x)\ge0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary upper-level stationarity condition for a local MPEC solution whose equilibrium solution map is represented by the strongly regular generalized equation (5.24), with an objective independent of the equilibrium multipliers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower-subdifferential necessary conditions for an abstract MPEC
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two alternative qualification regimes yielding a limiting-subdifferential coderivative-normal stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\bar x,\bar y)$ be a local solution of the abstract MPEC. Assume that $X,Y$ are Asplund spaces, $\varphi$ is lower semicontinuous around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\operatorname{gph}S$ is locally closed around $(\bar x,\bar y)$, and $\Omega$ is locally closed around $\bar x$. Then
\[
\exists(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y):\quad 0\in x^*+D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega)
\]
under either of these regimes: (i) all assumptions of the upper-subdifferential condition hold, $\varphi$ is SNEC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$, and
\[
(x_\infty^*,y_\infty^*)\in\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\quad 0\in x_\infty^*+D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y_\infty^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega)
\]
imply $x_\infty^*=y_\infty^*=0$; these additional assumptions hold automatically if $\varphi$ is locally Lipschitz around $(\bar x,\bar y)$. (ii) $S$ is SNC at $(\bar x,\bar y)$, $\Omega$ is SNC at $\bar x$, and
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(x_\infty^*,y_\infty^*)\in\partial^\infty\varphi(\bar x,\bar y),\quad x_1^*\in D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y_\infty^*),\\
&x_2^*\in N(\bar x;\Omega),\quad x_\infty^*+x_1^*+x_2^*=0
\end{aligned}
\]
imply $x_\infty^*=y_\infty^*=x_1^*=x_2^*=0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local abstract-MPEC solution satisfies a limiting-subdifferential coderivative-normal stationarity condition under either the upper-condition hypotheses plus SNEC and a singular-subgradient qualification, or SNC of both constraint objects plus the stronger decomposition qualification.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar y)\text{ is a local solution of the abstract MPEC}
\varphi\text{ is lower semicontinuous around }(\bar x,\bar y)
\operatorname{gph}S\text{ is locally closed around }(\bar x,\bar y)
\text{Either qualification regime (i) or qualification regime (ii) stated above holds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(x^*,y^*)\in\partial\varphi(\bar x,\bar y)\quad 0\in x^*+D_N^*S(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)+N(\bar x;\Omega).

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Normal-Cone Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-tolerance certificate separating distance to the constraint set from normal-cone criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper and lower semicontinuous. For \(\delta\geq0\), define the enlarged normal cone \(N_C^{\delta}(x)=\bigcup\{N_C(y):y\in C,\ \|y-x\|\leq\delta\}\). A point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-normal-cone stationary if \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\delta\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)+N_C^{\delta}(x))\leq\varepsilon\). When \(x\in C\) and \(\delta=0\), this reduces to the exact-cone residual \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)+N_C(x))\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate separately bounds infeasibility and the distance of zero from the objective subdifferential plus an exact or locally enlarged constraint normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leq\delta\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x)+N_C^{\delta}(x))\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: union of normals based at feasible points within delta of x

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate KKT Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsmooth KKT certificate with separate feasibility, stationarity, sign, and complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h(x)=0\), where the functions are locally Lipschitz. An \((\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_c)\)-KKT certificate consists of \(x\), multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), \(\mu\in\mathbb R^p\), and selections \(v_f\in\partial f(x)\), \(v_i\in\partial g_i(x)\), and \(w_j\in\partial h_j(x)\), satisfying \(\|v_f+\sum_i\lambda_i v_i+\sum_j\mu_jw_j\|\leq\varepsilon_s\), \(\|[g(x)]_+\|+\|h(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_f\), and \(\max_i|\lambda_i g_i(x)|\leq\varepsilon_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate KKT certificate jointly reports stationarity, primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, and complementarity errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residuals are bounded respectively by \(\varepsilon_s\), \(\varepsilon_f\), and \(\varepsilon_c\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Optimality Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic Fritz–John certificate that remains meaningful without a pointwise constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the locally Lipschitz program \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\) and \(h(x)=0\), a feasible point \(\bar x\) has a sequential Fritz–John certificate if there exist \(x^k\to\bar x\), scalars \(\alpha_k\geq0\), multipliers \(\lambda^k\geq0\), \(\mu^k\), and corresponding limiting subgradients such that \(\alpha_k+\|\lambda^k\|+\|\mu^k\|=1\), the Lagrangian stationarity residual tends to zero, \(\|[g(x^k)]_+\|+\|h(x^k)\|\to0\), and \(\lambda_i^k g_i(x^k)\to0\) for every \(i\). A KKT-type sequence additionally has \(\alpha_k\to1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential certificate uses nearby points and normalized Fritz–John multipliers whose stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residuals vanish; no pointwise constraint qualification is built into its definition.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\) are locally Lipschitz near the feasible point \(\bar x\).
The stationarity residual uses compatible selections from their limiting subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residuals converge to zero along a normalized multiplier sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Stationarity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate tolerances prevent one residual scale from concealing poor feasibility or poor criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_f(x)\geq0\) measure constraint violation and \(r_s(x)\geq0\) measure stationarity. An \((\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_s)\)-certificate requires \(r_f(x)\leq\varepsilon_f\) and \(r_s(x)\leq\varepsilon_s\). For weights \(a,b>0\), the scalar bound \(a r_f(x)+b r_s(x)\leq\varepsilon\) implies only \(r_f(x)\leq\varepsilon/a\) and \(r_s(x)\leq\varepsilon/b\). Conversely, the two componentwise bounds imply \(a r_f(x)+b r_s(x)\leq a\varepsilon_f+b\varepsilon_s\). Thus changing weights changes the certified tradeoff unless an additional error-bound relation links the residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility and stationarity should be reported separately: a weighted aggregate controls them only at weight-dependent accuracies unless an error bound couples the two residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a r_f+b r_s\leq\varepsilon\Rightarrow(r_f\leq\varepsilon/a,\ r_s\leq\varepsilon/b)\), while componentwise bounds imply the corresponding weighted bound.

children.title: Moreau-Envelope Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Smooth surrogate stationarity and its relationship to proximal points.

children.title: Moreau-Envelope Gradient-Norm Certificate
children.top_down_role: Stationarity measured through the gradient norm of a valid smooth envelope.

knowledge_statements.title: Moreau-Envelope Gradient-Norm Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakly convex finite-dimensional stationarity measured by the gradient of a differentiable Moreau envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and choose \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with \(1/0=+\infty\). Define \(f_\lambda(x)=\min_y\{f(y)+\|y-x\|^2/(2\lambda)\}\). The proximal minimizer \(P_\lambda(x)\) is unique, \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable, and \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\). Hence \(x\) has an \(\varepsilon\)-Moreau-envelope certificate precisely when \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weakly convex function and a valid smoothing parameter, the Moreau envelope is smooth; its gradient norm is the scaled displacement to the unique proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|=\lambda^{-1}\|x-P_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard differentiability formula for the Moreau envelope of a weakly convex function
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate and weak-convexity parameter regime fit the leaf, but the global uniqueness, differentiability, and gradient formula require an authoritative cited locator.

children.title: Proximal-Point Displacement Certificate
children.top_down_role: Stationarity measured by displacement from a point to its proximal image.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Point Displacement Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent weakly convex stationarity certificate expressed as unscaled distance to the proximal image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the weak-convexity and parameter assumptions ensuring that \(P_\lambda(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\{f(y)+\|y-x\|^2/(2\lambda)\}\) is single-valued, define the displacement \(d_\lambda(x)=\|x-P_\lambda(x)\|\). A point \(x\) has an \(\eta\)-proximal-displacement certificate when \(d_\lambda(x)\leq\eta\). Since \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\), this certificate is exactly equivalent to the Moreau-envelope bound \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\eta/\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal displacement and Moreau-envelope gradient norm carry the same information, differing only by the parameter factor λ.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_\lambda(x)\leq\eta\iff\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\eta/\lambda\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: immediate scaling identity between proximal displacement and envelope gradient

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displacement certificate and its scaling equivalence fit the exact terminal container, but they depend on an uncited Moreau-envelope gradient identity.

children.title: Envelope-to-Near-Point Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Conversion from envelope stationarity to subdifferential stationarity at a proximal point.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-to-Near-Point Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope criticality transfers to limiting-subdifferential criticality at the associated nearby proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, let \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), and set \(y=P_\lambda(x)\). Proximal optimality and weak convexity give \(v=\lambda^{-1}(x-y)=\nabla f_\lambda(x)\in\partial f(y)\). Consequently, if \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\), then \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon\). Thus envelope stationarity at \(x\) certifies ordinary limiting-subdifferential stationarity at a quantitatively nearby point \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small envelope gradient produces a proximal point within λε whose limiting subdifferential contains a vector of norm at most ε.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\Rightarrow\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proximal optimality inclusion and Moreau-gradient identity for weakly convex functions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly targets transfer to a nearby proximal point, but the proximal optimality inclusion and limiting-subdifferential conclusion lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Exact Proximal-Point Residual Certificate
children.top_down_role: Residual criticality based on an exact proximal point.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Proximal-Point Residual Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation yields a computable residual and a subgradient at the proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, with \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). For \(y=P_\lambda(x)\), define the exact proximal residual \(r_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-y)\). Then \(r_\lambda(x)\in\partial f(y)\), so \(\|r_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\). Moreover, \(r_\lambda(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=y\) and \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled displacement to an exact proximal point is a subgradient there; its norm certifies nearby stationarity and vanishes exactly at a stationary fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\lambda(x)\in\partial f(P_\lambda(x))\), with \(r_\lambda(x)=0\iff0\in\partial f(x)\).

children.title: Inexact Proximal Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates separating proximal-subproblem error from outer stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-component certificate separating inner proximal optimality error from outer displacement residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and take \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). An inexact proximal certificate at \(x\) consists of \(y\), an error \(e\), and the outer residual \(r=\lambda^{-1}(x-y)\), such that \(e\in\partial f(y)+(y-x)/\lambda\), \(\|e\|\leq\eta\), and \(\|r\|\leq\varepsilon\). The inclusion gives \(r+e\in\partial f(y)\); hence \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon+\eta\) and \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact proximal certificate records inner-solve error and outer displacement separately; together they bound subdifferential stationarity at the computed proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(y))\leq\varepsilon+\eta\) and \(\|x-y\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\).

children.title: Resolvent-Fixed-Point Residual Pair

children.title: Resolvent Residuals
children.top_down_role: Operator-resolvent representations of proximal stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone-inclusion residual obtained by evaluating the resolvent of a maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) be maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space and let \(\lambda>0\). Its resolvent \(J_{\lambda A}=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}\) is single-valued, and the scaled resolvent residual is \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-J_{\lambda A}x)\). By the resolvent definition, \(R_{\lambda A}(x)\in A(J_{\lambda A}x)\). Therefore \(\|R_{\lambda A}(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an element of \(A\) with norm at most \(\varepsilon\) at the nearby point \(J_{\lambda A}x\), and \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=0\) exactly when \(0\in A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled resolvent displacement belongs to the operator at the resolvent point, and it vanishes exactly at solutions of the monotone inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\lambda A}(x)\in A(J_{\lambda A}x)\) and \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=0\iff0\in A(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining identity of the resolvent of a maximal monotone operator

children.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual certificates measuring failure of a proximal or resolvent fixed-point relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unscaled residual certifying approximate fixed points of the resolvent and solutions of the associated inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) be maximal monotone, let \(\lambda>0\), and define the fixed-point residual \(F_{\lambda A}(x)=x-J_{\lambda A}x\). A bound \(\|F_{\lambda A}(x)\|\leq\eta\) certifies that \(x\) is an \(\eta\)-approximate fixed point of the resolvent. Exactly, \(F_{\lambda A}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=J_{\lambda A}x\), which is equivalent to \(0\in A(x)\). The scaled resolvent residual satisfies \(R_{\lambda A}(x)=\lambda^{-1}F_{\lambda A}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distance from a point to its resolvent image is a fixed-point residual; zero residual is equivalent to solving the monotone inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\lambda A}(x)=0\iff x=J_{\lambda A}x\iff0\in A(x)\), and \(R_{\lambda A}=\lambda^{-1}F_{\lambda A}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic fixed-point characterization of resolvent zeros
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Residual Scaling Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes governing comparability between resolvent and fixed-point residual magnitudes.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\lambda(x)=\lambda\nabla f_\lambda(x)\), so \(\|r_\lambda(x)\|=\lambda\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\) and either residual vanishes exactly when the other does.

notation.meaning: Proximal mapping of f with parameter lambda.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean weakly convex Moreau envelopes in the single-valued proximal regime.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), strong convexity of the proximal subproblem makes \(P_\lambda(x)\) single-valued, and the Moreau envelope is continuously differentiable with \[\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-P_\lambda(x)\bigr)=\lambda^{-1}r_\lambda(x).\] Consequently, the resolvent fixed-point residual and the envelope-gradient residual contain identical stationarity information, differing only by the positive scale factor \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal fixed-point residual equals the envelope gradient multiplied by the proximal parameter, so both residuals detect exactly the same stationary points.

children.title: Structured Proximal Residuals

children.title: Prox-Linear Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Model-gradient and proximal residuals for composite objectives.

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x)\), where \(h\) is proper closed convex, \(c\) is continuously differentiable, and \(g\) is proper closed convex.
The displayed prox-linear subproblem has a minimizer for the chosen \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_t(x)=0\) exactly when \(0\in \nabla c(x)^\top\partial h(c(x))+\partial g(x)\), subject to the convex-composite subdifferential chain rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-composite Euclidean prox-linear stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[d_t(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{h\bigl(c(x)+\nabla c(x)d\bigr)+g(x+d)+\frac{1}{2t}\|d\|^2\right\},\qquad G_t(x)=-t^{-1}d_t(x).\] The vector \(G_t(x)\) is a verifiable prox-linear residual. In particular, \(G_t(x)=0\) if and only if \[0\in \nabla c(x)^\top\partial h(c(x))+\partial g(x),\] whenever the standard convex-composite chain rule is valid at \(x\). Thus a zero residual certifies first-order stationarity of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled prox-linear step is a stationarity residual; it vanishes exactly when the convex-composite first-order inclusion holds under the chain rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Residual Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate has the correct local role and is mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source is supplied for the precise prox-linear subproblem, the zero-residual equivalence, or the required convex-composite chain-rule qualification.

children.title: Model-Based Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Stationarity measures produced by local approximation models.

assumptions_latex: For each base point \(x\), \(m_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies \(m_x(x)=f(x)\).
For \(t>0\), the regularized model subproblem has a selected minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable quantity \(R_t(x)=t^{-1}(x-T_t(x))\) is zero exactly when \(x\) minimizes its regularized local model; under first-order model consistency, this certifies stationarity of \(f\).

notation.meaning: Local approximation model of f at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic proximal regularization of a first-order consistent local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \[T_t(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{m_x(y)+\frac{1}{2t}\|y-x\|^2\right\},\qquad R_t(x)=t^{-1}\bigl(x-T_t(x)\bigr).\] Then \(R_t(x)=0\) if and only if the selected regularized model point equals its base point. If the model is first-order consistent in the sense that \(\partial m_x(x)=\partial f(x)\) for the chosen subdifferential, this equality yields \(0\in\partial f(x)\). Hence \(R_t(x)\) is a directly checkable model-based stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled displacement from the base point to a regularized model minimizer is a residual; zero certifies stationarity when model and objective subdifferentials agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Based Residual Certificates

children.title: Convex-Set Constrained Proximal Residuals
children.top_down_role: Proximal certificates after incorporating a convex feasible-set indicator.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(\lambda>0\).
At the point under consideration, the convex subdifferential sum rule gives \(\partial(f+\delta_C)(x)=\partial f(x)+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in C\), \(R_{\lambda,C}(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Indicator of the feasible set C.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex objectives over closed convex feasible sets represented through indicator functions.

source_refs.locator: 6.1.1 The convex constrained case p. 324

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), define \[P_{\lambda,C}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\},\qquad R_{\lambda,C}(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-P_{\lambda,C}(x)\bigr).\] For every \(x\in C\), the constrained proximal residual satisfies \[R_{\lambda,C}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(x)+N_C(x),\] provided the stated convex subdifferential sum rule holds at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex objective over a closed convex set, the constrained proximal residual vanishes exactly when the convex subgradient and normal-cone stationarity inclusion holds, subject to the stated sum rule.

children.title: Weak-Convexity Applicability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing the validity and interpretation of envelope and proximal certificates.

children.title: Envelope-Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter ranges supporting a single-valued proximal map and smooth-envelope interpretation.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The strict regime \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\) guarantees a single-valued proximal map and a continuously differentiable Moreau envelope with \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniform parameter regime implied solely by the weak-convexity modulus.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The envelope parameter must satisfy \[0<\lambda<\frac{1}{\rho},\] where \(1/0=+\infty\). In this regime, the function \(y\mapsto f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\) is strongly convex for every \(x\), so \(P_\lambda(x)\) is uniquely defined. Moreover, \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable and \[\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-P_\lambda(x)\bigr).\] At or beyond \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), weak convexity alone does not ensure either uniqueness or this smooth-envelope representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rho-weakly convex function, parameters strictly below 1/rho guarantee a unique proximal point and the smooth Moreau-envelope gradient formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Parameter Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

children.title: Proximal-Map Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Failure of single-valued proximal certificate representations outside valid regimes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=\mathbb{R}\), so the proximal map is not single-valued at the boundary parameter.

notation.meaning: Proximal objective at base point x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional boundary example showing sharp loss of proximal uniqueness.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex because \(f(y)+(\rho/2)y^2=0\). At \(x=0\) and \(\lambda=\rho^{-1}\), its proximal objective is \[q_0(y)=-\frac{\rho}{2}y^2+\frac{1}{2\lambda}y^2=0\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}.\] Hence every \(y\in\mathbb{R}\) minimizes the subproblem, and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=\mathbb{R}\). A single-valued residual or envelope-gradient representation therefore cannot be inferred at the boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At lambda equal to 1/rho, a negative quadratic has every real number as a proximal point at zero, destroying residual uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Map Nonuniqueness

children.title: Stationary but Nonoptimal Weakly Convex Points
children.top_down_role: Limits of proximal and envelope stationarity as an optimality guarantee.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial f(0)\) and \(\nabla f_\lambda(0)=0\), although \(0\) is neither a local nor a global minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth one-dimensional example separating weakly convex stationarity from optimality.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.3 Weakly convex functions p. 214

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is \(2\)-weakly convex and satisfies \(f'(0)=0\). For \(0<\lambda<1/2\), the proximal objective at zero is \[f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}y^2=\left(\frac{1}{2\lambda}-1\right)y^2,\] whose unique minimizer is \(P_\lambda(0)=0\). Thus \(\nabla f_\lambda(0)=\lambda^{-1}(0-P_\lambda(0))=0\). Nevertheless, \(f(y)<f(0)\) for every \(y\ne0\), so zero is a strict local maximum rather than a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weakly convex function minus x squared has zero proximal and envelope residual at zero, but zero is a strict maximum, not a minimum.

children.title: Generalized-Pseudoconvex Optimality Tests
children.top_down_role: Stationarity-to-global-optimality routes under generalized pseudoconvexity.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz on an open neighborhood of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(0\in\partial_C f(\bar x)\), then \(f(y)\ge f(\bar x)\) for every \(y\in C\); hence \(\bar x\) is a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke-pseudoconvex sufficiency for unconstrained stationarity on a convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\in C\) satisfy \(0\in\partial_C f(\bar x)\). By the support representation of the Clarke derivative, \[f^{\circ}(\bar x;y-\bar x)=\max_{v\in\partial_C f(\bar x)}\langle v,y-\bar x\rangle\ge0\qquad\text{for every }y\in C.\] Clarke pseudoconvexity, expressed by the second assumption, therefore gives \(f(y)\ge f(\bar x)\) for all \(y\in C\). Thus Clarke stationarity is a sufficient certificate of global optimality under this generalized-pseudoconvex structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Clarke-pseudoconvex locally Lipschitz function, every Clarke-stationary point is a global minimizer on the convex domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Pseudoconvex Optimality Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is plausible for the explicitly stated Clarke-pseudoconvex implication, but no source identifies this generalized-pseudoconvex variant or supports the exact hypotheses. The statement also contains proof-style reasoning that must be removed once the sourced theorem formulation is fixed.

children.title: Generalized-Quasiconvex Optimality Tests
children.top_down_role: Directional and level-set tests under generalized quasiconvexity.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is locally Lipschitz on a neighborhood of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized directional quasiconvexity test is \(f(y)\le f(x)\Rightarrow f^{\circ}(x;y-x)\le0\) for all \(x,y\in C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clarke directional formulation tied to lower level sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A locally Lipschitz function satisfies the Clarke directional quasiconvexity test on \(C\) when, for every \(x\in C\), \[y\in L_f(x)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f^{\circ}(x;y-x)\le0\qquad\text{for every }y\in C.\] Equivalently, every direction from \(x\) toward a point in its lower level set has nonpositive Clarke generalized directional derivative. This is a structural test; unlike pseudoconvexity, it does not by itself make the inclusion \(0\in\partial_C f(x)\) sufficient for global minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directional quasiconvexity requires every direction toward a no-higher objective value to have nonpositive Clarke directional derivative; this alone does not make stationarity sufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Quasiconvex Optimality Tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for treating the displayed Clarke directional implication as the intended generalized-quasiconvex condition. Clarke, Dini, and other directional formulations are not interchangeable without regularity assumptions, so the exact mathematical variant cannot be confirmed.

children.title: Generalized-Convexity Sufficiency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure of stationarity-based sufficiency when the required generalized-convex structure is absent.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(0\in\partial_C f(0)\), the point \(0\) is not a minimizer; hence stationarity is insufficient without an appropriate generalized-pseudoconvex assumption.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth scalar counterexample; quasiconvexity alone does not upgrade stationarity to optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The function \(f\) is smooth, increasing, and therefore quasiconvex, while \(\partial_C f(0)=\{0\}\). Nevertheless, for every \(y<0\), \(f(y)<f(0)=0\), so zero is not a local or global minimizer. Moreover, taking \(x=0\) and \(y=-1\) gives \(f'(0)(y-x)=0\) but \(f(y)<f(x)\), violating the pseudoconvex implication. Thus stationarity-based global sufficiency fails when the stronger generalized-convex structure is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quasiconvex function x cubed is stationary at zero but decreases to its left, showing that quasiconvexity alone does not make stationarity sufficient.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local generalized-order optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The generating set need not be convex or have nonempty interior. The definition includes standard scalar local optimality and conventional vector-optimality notions as special cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X,Z\) be Banach spaces, \(f:X	o Z\), and \(0\in\Theta\subset Z\). A point \( ar x\in X\) is locally \((f,\Theta)\)-optimal if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \( ar x\) and a sequence \(z_k	o0\) in \(Z\) such that \[f(x)-f( ar x)
otin\Theta-z_k\qquad	ext{for every }x\in U	ext{ and }k\in\mathbb N.\] The set \(\Theta\) induces the preference \(z_1\preceq_\Theta z_2\iff z_1-z_2\in\Theta\). For \(Z=\mathbb R\) and \(\Theta=\mathbb R_-\), this is ordinary local optimality. If \(\Theta\) is a convex cone with \(\operatorname{ri}\Theta
e\varnothing\), the condition includes absence of \(x\in U\) satisfying \(f(x)-f( ar x)\in\operatorname{ri}\Theta\), by taking \(z_k=-z_0/k\) for some \(z_0\in\operatorname{ri}\Theta\). Weak Pareto optimality uses \(\operatorname{int}\Theta\); Pareto optimality excludes \(x\in U\) for which \(f(x)-f( ar x)\in\Theta\) and \(f( ar x)-f(x)
otin\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Banach-space-valued objective and an ordering generator containing zero, a point is locally generalized-order optimal when one neighborhood and a vanishing sequence of order perturbations exclude every nearby objective difference from every shifted ordering set. No convexity or interior assumption on the generator is required. The notion reduces to ordinary scalar local optimality and encompasses relative-interior, weak Pareto, and Pareto variants under their stated cone assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is locally }(f,\Theta)\text{-optimal}\iff\exists U\ni\bar x,\ \exists(z_k)\subset Z,\ z_k\to0:\ \forall x\in U,\ \forall k\in\mathbb N,\ f(x)-f(\bar x)\notin\Theta-z_k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Specialized radial-directional sufficient conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate sufficient local-minimality conditions for pessimistic and optimistic bilevel solution functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the pessimistic solution function, if \(\varphi_p(x^0)=\varphi_p(x^0;r)\) and \(d\varphi_{p,x^0}(r)>\gamma>0\) for every \(r\), then \(x^0\in\operatorname{locmin}\varphi_p\). For the optimistic solution function, if, for every \(r\), either \(\varphi_o(x^0)<\varphi_o(x^0;r)\) or \(d\varphi_{o,x^0}(r)>0\), then \(x^0\in\operatorname{locmin}\varphi_o\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stated uniform equality and positive-derivative condition is sufficient for pessimistic local minimality. For the optimistic function, every direction must have either a strictly larger radial limit or a positive radial-directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi_p\) and \(\varphi_o\) are the pessimistic and optimistic solution functions, respectively.
For the pessimistic implication, \(\varphi_p(x^0)=\varphi_p(x^0;r)\) and \(d\varphi_{p,x^0}(r)>\gamma>0\) hold for every \(r\).
For the optimistic implication, the stated disjunction holds for every \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Respectively, \(x^0\in\operatorname{locmin}\varphi_p\) and \(x^0\in\operatorname{locmin}\varphi_o\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Locally satiated, almost transitive, and closed preferences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: These properties are defined through strict lower level sets. Local satiation may hold even when almost transitivity fails, including for some cone-generated generalized Pareto preferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a preference relation \(\prec\) on \(Z\), define \(\mathcal L(z):=\{u\in Z\mid u\prec z\}\). The relation is locally satiated around \(\bar z\) if there exists a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar z\) such that \(z\in\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(z)\) for every \(z\in V\). It is almost transitive on \(Z\) if \[\forall u,z\in Z,\ u\prec z,\ \forall v\in\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(u):\quad v\prec z.\] It is closed around \(\bar z\) precisely when it is both locally satiated around \(\bar z\) and almost transitive on \(Z\). A generalized Pareto preference generated by a closed cone \(\Theta\subset Z\) is given by \(z_1\prec z_2\iff z_1-z_2\in\Theta\) and \(z_1\ne z_2\); such preferences need not be almost transitive without further conditions on \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strict lower level set at z consists of all points preferred to z. A preference is locally satiated near a reference point when every nearby point lies in the closure of its own lower level set. It is almost transitive when anything in the closure of the lower level set of a point preferred to z is also preferred to z. A preference is closed near the reference point when both properties hold. Cone-generated generalized Pareto preferences may fail almost transitivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \prec\text{ is closed around }\bar z\iff\bigl[\exists V\ni\bar z\ \forall z\in V:\ z\in\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(z)\bigr]\ \land\ \bigl[\forall u\prec z\ \forall v\in\operatorname{cl}\mathcal L(u):\ v\prec z\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epsilon-Optimal Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate global optimality measured by an additive objective-value tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a point \(\bar x\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution of \(\min_{x\in\Phi}f(x)\) if \[\bar x\in\Phi\qquad\text{and}\qquad f(\bar x)\le \inf_{x\in\Phi}f(x)+\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative tolerance epsilon, a feasible point is epsilon-optimal when its objective value is no more than epsilon above the infimum over the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(\bar x)\le\inf_{x\in\Phi}f(x)+\varepsilon

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relaxed Unconstrained Direction-Set Optimality Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary relaxed condition for a locally Lipschitz local minimizer, with global sufficiency under pseudoconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be locally Lipschitz at \(x^*\in\mathbb{R}^n\). If \(f\) attains a local minimum at \(x^*\), then \(D_S^\circ(x^*)=D_S(x^*)=\{0\}\). If, in addition, \(f\) is \(f^\circ\)-pseudoconvex, then this equality is sufficient for \(x^*\) to be a global minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a local minimizer of a locally Lipschitz function, both specified relaxed direction sets equal the zero set. Under f-circ-pseudoconvexity, that equality is also sufficient for global minimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local minimizer}\Rightarrow D_S^\circ(x^*)=D_S(x^*)=\{0\};\quad f\text{ additionally }f^\circ\text{-pseudoconvex}\Rightarrow\left(D_S^\circ(x^*)=D_S(x^*)=\{0\}\Rightarrow x^*\text{ global minimizer}\right)

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Analytical-Constraint Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An ε-Clarke–KKT certificate for locally Lipschitz inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be locally Lipschitz, and let \(x\) satisfy \(g_i(x)\leq0\). For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), an \(\varepsilon\)-relaxed analytical-constraint certificate consists of multipliers \(\lambda_i\geq0\), subgradients \(v_0\in\partial_C f(x)\), and \(v_i\in\partial_C g_i(x)\) such that
\[\left\|v_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i v_i\right\|\leq\varepsilon,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i|g_i(x)|\leq\varepsilon.\]
It certifies approximate Clarke stationarity and approximate complementarity; by itself it does not certify local or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers and Clarke subgradients certify relaxed constrained stationarity when the Lagrangian residual and total complementarity error are at most ε.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are locally Lipschitz near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_C f(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i\partial_C g_i(x))\leq\varepsilon\) with approximate complementarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient multiplier condition for a pseudoconvex objective with quasiconvex inequality functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Problem (4.11) satisfies the Cottle constraint qualification at \(x^*\in S\). Then \(x^*\) is a global optimum of Problem (4.11) if and only if there exist multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) such that \(\lambda_i g_i(x^*)=0\) for every \(i\) and \(0\in\partial f(x^*)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\partial g_i(x^*)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Quasidifferential Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order necessary condition for a finite-dimensional quasidifferentiable local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar x\) and has quasidifferential \([A,B]\), where \(A,B\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets and
\[f'(\bar x;d)=\max_{a\in A}\langle a,d\rangle+\min_{b\in B}\langle b,d\rangle.\]
If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer, then \(f'(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\). Equivalently,
\[-B\subseteq A.\]
This inclusion is quasidifferential stationarity and is generally necessary, not sufficient, for local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an unconstrained quasidifferentiable local minimum, every directional derivative is nonnegative, equivalently the negative upper quasidifferential lies inside the lower one.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(B\) are nonempty compact convex subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for all \(d\), equivalently \(-B\subseteq A\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The necessary condition and inclusion equivalence are mathematically consistent under the displayed quasidifferential convention, and the condition kind fits the leaf. No inspectable source supports that convention or result.

children.title: Quasidifferential Descent Certificates
children.top_down_role: Separation between quasidifferential stationarity and explicit descent regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasidifferential Descent Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A directly verifiable strict-descent certificate from quasidifferential components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([A,B]\) represent the quasidifferential of \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) at \(x\). A pair \((b,d)\in B\times\mathbb R^n\) is a strict quasidifferential descent certificate if
\[\max_{a\in A}\langle a,d\rangle+\langle b,d\rangle<0.\]
Because
\[f'(x;d)=\max_{a\in A}\langle a,d\rangle+\min_{u\in B}\langle u,d\rangle,\]
the displayed inequality implies \(f'(x;d)<0\). In particular, if some \(b\in B\) satisfies \(-b\notin A\), strong separation supplies such a direction \(d\), so \(x\) cannot be a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper component and a direction whose combined support value is negative certify strict directional descent and rule out local minimality.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\subset\mathbb R^n\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(x;d)<0\), hence \(x\) is not a local minimizer.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed pair is a valid strict-descent certificate under the displayed quasidifferential convention, and the content kind fits the leaf. An authoritative locator is required to establish the convention and separation-based conclusion.

children.title: Constrained Quasidifferential Conditions

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Quasidifferential Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A primal directional condition for quasidifferentiable inequality-constrained problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\), where \(f,g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) are Hadamard directionally differentiable at a feasible point \(\bar x\) and their directional derivatives admit quasidifferential representations. Let \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). If \(\bar x\) is a local minimizer, there is no direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying simultaneously
\[f'(\bar x;d)<0,\qquad g_i'(\bar x;d)<0\quad\text{for every }i\in I(\bar x).\]
Thus every strict first-order feasible direction obeys \(f'(\bar x;d)\geq0\). Multiplier reformulations require an additional quasidifferential constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained local minimum admits no direction that strictly decreases both the objective and every active quasidifferentiable constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is feasible and \(f,g_i\) are Hadamard directionally differentiable there.
Each directional derivative has a finite-dimensional quasidifferential representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i'(\bar x;d)<0\) for all \(i\in I(\bar x)\) implies \(f'(\bar x;d)\geq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict directional exclusion is plausible for the stated finite-dimensional Hadamard setting and is correctly distinguished from multiplier conditions, but no source verifies the exact constrained quasidifferential formulation or its hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasidifferentiable constraint sets, regularity, and feasible directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a single-inequality quasidifferentiable set, its boundary regularity condition, and the resulting feasible-direction identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ is quasidifferentiable if $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid h(x)\leq0\}$ for a quasidifferentiable function $h$. For $x\in\Omega$, let $\gamma_1(x)=\{g\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid h'(x;g)<0\}$ and $\Gamma_1(x)=\{g\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid h'(x;g)\leq0\}$. At a boundary point $h(x)=0$, regularity means $\operatorname{cl}\gamma_1(x)=\Gamma_1(x)$. If $h(x)<0$, then the feasible-direction cone is $\Gamma(x)=\mathbb{R}^n$; if $h(x)=0$ and regularity holds, then $\Gamma(x)=\Gamma_1(x)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasidifferentiable set is a sublevel set of a quasidifferentiable function. At a boundary point, regularity equates the closure of the strict linearized cone with the nonstrict linearized cone. Under regularity, the latter is the feasible-direction cone; at an interior point every direction is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h(x)<0\Rightarrow\Gamma(x)=\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad h(x)=0\ \land\ \operatorname{cl}\gamma_1(x)=\Gamma_1(x)\Rightarrow\Gamma(x)=\Gamma_1(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Necessary Quasidifferential Condition for One Active Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A first-order necessary condition for minimization over a quasidifferentiable inequality set at an active regular boundary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid h(x)\le 0\}\). Suppose \(f\) and \(h\) are locally Lipschitz continuous and quasidifferentiable in a neighborhood of \(x^*\in\Omega\), \(h(x^*)=0\), and the regularity condition holds at \(x^*\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity Condition for a Quasidifferentiable Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary regularity expressed through strict and non-strict linearized feasible-direction sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid h(y)\le 0\}\), let \(x\in\Omega\) satisfy \(h(x)=0\), and define \(\gamma_1(x)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid h'(x;d)<0\}\) and \(\gamma_2(x)=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid h'(x;d)\le 0\}\). children.title: Epsilon-Quasidifferential Optimality
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-based quasidifferential criticality and optimality conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Quasidifferential Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-tolerant quasidifferential stationarity in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \([A,B]\) be a quasidifferential of \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) at \(x\), with \(A,B\) nonempty compact convex, and let \(\varepsilon\geq0\). The point \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-quasidifferentially stationary when
\[-B\subseteq A+\varepsilon\mathbb B.\]
Equivalently, its directional derivative satisfies
\[f'(x;d)\geq-\varepsilon\|d\|\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n.\]
For \(\varepsilon=0\) this reduces to exact quasidifferential stationarity. For positive tolerance it excludes directions having normalized first-order decrease greater than \(\varepsilon\), but it does not alone guarantee approximate objective optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epsilon-stationarity means the negative upper quasidifferential lies within ε of the lower component, equivalently no unit direction decreases faster than ε.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\) are nonempty compact convex sets and \(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-B\subseteq A+\varepsilon\mathbb B\), equivalently \(f'(x;d)\geq-\varepsilon\|d\|\) for every \(d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set inclusion and directional inequality are equivalent under the displayed Euclidean quasidifferential convention, and condition is the appropriate kind. The epsilon convention lacks authoritative support.

children.title: Codifferential Stationarity

knowledge_statements.title: Codifferential Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity expressed through normalized lower and upper codifferential slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be codifferentiable at \(x\), with lower and upper codifferentials \(\underline d f(x),\overline d f(x)\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n\), normalized by
\[\max_{(a,v)\in\underline d f(x)}a=0,\qquad \min_{(b,w)\in\overline d f(x)}b=0.\]
Define \(A_0=\{v:(0,v)\in\underline d f(x)\}\) and \(B_0=\{w:(0,w)\in\overline d f(x)\}\). If \(x\) is an unconstrained local minimizer, then
\[-B_0\subseteq A_0.\]
Equivalently, every upper zero-slice vector \(w\) is balanced by a lower zero-slice vector \(-w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a codifferentiable local minimum, every vector in the normalized upper zero slice has its negative in the lower zero slice.
assumptions_latex: The lower and upper codifferentials are nonempty compact convex sets with the displayed normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-B_0\subseteq A_0\).

notation.meaning: zero-scalar slices of the two codifferentials

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stationarity condition fits the leaf, but its validity depends on the precise codifferential normalization and on whether the directional derivative is represented by the stated zero slices. Those conventions require a specific source.

children.title: Codifferential Descent Conditions
children.top_down_role: Descent certificates extracted from codifferential structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Codifferential Descent Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A strict-descent test using normalized codifferential zero slices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the normalized codifferential notation \(A_0,B_0\), a pair \((w,d)\in B_0\times\mathbb R^n\) is a codifferential descent certificate if
\[\max_{v\in A_0}\langle v,d\rangle+\langle w,d\rangle<0.\]
The codifferential directional expansion then yields
\[f'(x;d)\leq\max_{v\in A_0}\langle v,d\rangle+\langle w,d\rangle<0,\]
so \(d\) is a strict descent direction. In particular, the failure \(-B_0\subseteq A_0\) produces such a certificate by strong separation and rules out local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-slice upper vector and separating direction certify negative directional derivative, thereby ruling out local minimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is codifferentiable at \(x\) with normalized compact convex codifferentials.
\(A_0\) and \(B_0\) are the corresponding zero-scalar slices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f'(x;d)<0\), hence \(x\) is not a local minimizer.

notation.meaning: normalized lower and upper zero slices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content is appropriately a descent certificate, but the asserted upper estimate for the directional derivative depends on an uncited codifferential expansion and zero-slice convention.
